name: T-Visa (I-914)
summary: T nonimmigrant status for victims of a severe form of trafficking in persons, with optional law enforcement declaration (Supplement B) and derivative family members (Supplement A).
confidentialityNote: Protected by 8 U.S.C. 1367. Restricted case. Never contact or name the traffickers in any notice.

forms.title: Application for Family Member of T-1 Recipient
forms.note: One per family member; may also be filed later (I-914 Instructions).

forms.title: Declaration for Trafficking Victim
forms.note: Optional. Completed and signed by a law enforcement official, never auto-filled (I-914B Instructions 09/14/26).

forms.title: Application for Advance Permission to Enter as a Nonimmigrant
forms.note: Waiver of inadmissibility if needed; attorney decides.

questions.label: Is it safe for us to call, text or mail you at the address and phone you gave?
Describe what happened: how you were recruited, what you were forced to do, how long, who was responsible, and how you got away
How is your being in the U.S. connected to the trafficking?
What harm do you fear if you are sent back? (danger, medical needs, loss of services, retaliation)
Have you reported the trafficking or helped police, FBI, DOL or prosecutors?
Agency, officer name, case number and what you did to help
Do you have (or can you get) a signed Supplement B from law enforcement?
If you could not help law enforcement, was it because of physical or psychological trauma, or were you under 18?
Do you want to include family members (Supplement A)?
Staff only: any ground of inadmissibility to waive (I-192)?

checklist.label: Your personal statement (required; staff will help you write it)
checklist.help: Describes the trafficking, how your presence relates to it, the hardship you fear, and your cooperation with law enforcement.

checklist.label: Any document showing how you entered the U.S.
checklist.help: Required if you have it or can get it.
checklist.source: I-914 Instructions 09/14/26, Evidence to Establish T Nonimmigrant Status

checklist.label: Signed Supplement B from a law enforcement officer
Proof you helped law enforcement (police reports, court documents, subpoenas, travel reimbursement forms, Continued Presence)
Evidence of trauma (statement from a doctor, counselor, social worker or victim advocate; medical records)
Proof of age (birth certificate or passport) if under 18
Other evidence of the trafficking (messages, pay records, photos, news articles, witness statements)
checklist.source: I-914 Instructions 09/14/26, any credible evidence (8 CFR 214.204(l))

checklist.label: Relationship documents for each family member (marriage and birth certificates)
checklist.source: I-914 Instructions 09/14/26, Evidence to Establish Derivative T Nonimmigrant Status

coverLetter.re: Form I-914, Application for T Nonimmigrant Status - CONFIDENTIAL, protected under 8 U.S.C. 1367
coverLetter.request: We respectfully submit the enclosed Form I-914 on behalf of {{givenName}} {{familyName}}, a victim of a severe form of trafficking in persons ({{traffickingType}}).
points: The applicant is or has been a victim of a severe form of trafficking in persons.
The applicant is physically present in the United States on account of trafficking.
The applicant has complied with reasonable requests for assistance from law enforcement, or an exception applies.
The applicant would suffer extreme hardship involving unusual and severe harm upon removal.
